paper.title_en: Reconstructing thermodynamics from quantum Fisher information
paper.abstract_en: We explore the possibility that thermodynamic structure can be reconstructed from geometric properties of quantum states. Motivated by recent results showing that equilibrium features can be diagnosed from geometric observables, we investigate whether quantities such as the quantum Fisher information encode sufficient information to generate thermodynamic potentials. We show that, under suitable consistency conditions, geometric data determine fluctuation relations and constrain the form of the partition function. This suggests a reformulation of thermodynamics in which geometry plays a primary role, providing a bridge between quantum information theory, statistical mechanics, and inverse problems in physics.
